A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoB research. The main text, figures, tables, algorithms, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including content moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original image- and video-understanding evaluations, latency measurements, parameter ablations, and token-selection visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluations without the coupling prior, detailed covering-fold results, and computation-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The core normalized nearest-neighbor covering and farthest-point sampling procedures, including Algorithms 1–2, are unchanged. Appendix D.4 adds a deployment adaptation that calibrates a coupling threshold and selects budget configurations per incoming sample. Further adaptation using a running threshold remains a proposed extension.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten image-understanding and four video-understanding benchmarks. The new discussion of open-domain operation, language compression, and RAG does not report evaluations on additional tasks or populations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in the corresponding main and appendix comparisons, including the broader baseline set in v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 5. DART and TwigVLM receive publication-label updates. The added prior-free rows are MoB ablations.

E3.justification: Section C.4 adds a benchmark-independent configuration without an eta prior, specifying Kp and k at the existing pruning budgets. Tables 6–7 document detailed k sweeps and FLOP comparisons with specified token dimensions. The original benchmark-group configurations, models, and pruning layers are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands checks of MoB's practical dependencies: Tables 2 and 5 test performance without the coupling prior, Table 6 examines detailed k sensitivity on GQA and TextVQA, and Table 7 separates coupling-estimation, pruning, and forward-pass costs. The existing budget, pruning-layer, and visualization analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 1234 in Section C.4. Neither reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty across runs. The retained coupling-distribution plots characterize input variation rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds a substantial result block without the eta prior: relative performance is 100.2%, 99.2%, and 96.3% at K=192, 128, and 64. It also adds detailed k-sweep scores and FLOP breakdowns. Original MoB results, now labeled with the prior, and corresponding baseline, Qwen2-VL, and video scores are unchanged; the additions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The main assumptions, lemmas, theorems, and proofs are retained. v2 corrects the inner distance in Equation E5-1 from ||p-s'_p|| to ||p-v|| and adds a covering-based stability argument involving Kp>=kL in Appendix D.3. The rewritten expression for D1 is algebraically equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about the Hausdorff error bound, objective trade-off, MoB's guarantees and scalability, and headline performance. The new controls support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds possible language-domain applications and explicitly warns that misestimating coupling can produce suboptimal configurations. Appendices D.2–D.4 add interpretations of selected tokens, k sensitivity, and online computation costs, plus qualifications and possible extensions for deployment.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository address in the abstract, explicit prior-free hyperparameters, and calibration and online-selection instructions. The existing hardware, software versions, evaluation framework, and seed disclosures remain unchanged. Repository availability is stated by the PDF but was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to TokenButler, value-aware KV-cache reduction, and Johnson–Lindenstrauss dimensionality reduction when discussing optional acceleration techniques in Appendix D.4. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes Appendix A into explicit impact and limitation paragraphs, expands Section C.4, and adds explanatory subsections D.3–D.4. It also updates authorship, affiliations, acknowledgments, and publication information. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a notation table and two analysis tables, expands the accuracy tables with prior-free rows, shades theorem statements, and adjusts figure placement. Figure 1's comparison annotations are corrected to refer explicitly to MustDrop. Existing plots and token-selection visualizations are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The prior-free controls, sensitivity results, and cost breakdown make MoB's dependence on benchmark priors and practical overhead easier to assess. The notation table and code pointer improve usability. These gains are limited by the unvalidated online deployment recipe and the new D.3 stability argument, whose Kp>=kL condition is not reconciled with Algorithm 1's candidate-budget constraints.
